instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file, with its updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures (i.e., a periodic spending report).
Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, which is triannual.
The statute specifies filings on the last day of January, May, and September (three times per year), not once annually.
The statute sets three fixed filing dates per year (January/May/September) rather than monthly filings.
Filing is required three times per year (January, May, September), not quarterly (four times per year).
The statute requires triannual updated registration statements (and accompanying expenditure statements), not semiannual statements.
The only periodic cadence specified for updated registration/expenditure statements is the last day of January, May, and September.
An employer's statement must show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.

The statutory definition of 'expenditure' includes gifts and items such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, which are the types of spending reported in expenditure statements.

For employer expenditure statements, 'expenditures' expressly do not include 'the compensation paid to legislative agents engaged by an employer,' so compensation is not reported as an expenditure item.
The statute excludes 'the expenses of maintaining office facilities' from the definition of reportable expenditures on an employer statement, indicating indirect/overhead costs are not included.
Section 101.73 prescribes reporting of expenditures and totals but does not require an employer expenditure statement to list the names of legislative agents engaged.
The updated registration statement filed with the employer's report must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.

The employer’s initial registration requires only a 'brief description of the type of legislation,' and the periodic update requires listing specific bills/resolutions, not general issue areas on the expenditure statement.
Neither the updated registration statement nor the expenditure statement requires reporting of lobbying contacts; they require listing bills/resolutions and expenditures.
Employer expenditure statements are focused on expenditure totals and, when applicable, recipient-specific expenditure details, without a requirement to include legislative agent names.
Section 101.73 does not require employer expenditure statements to include legislative agent addresses or other contact information.

Section 101.73 specifies expenditure reporting requirements and does not require inclusion of the employer’s name/address as part of the expenditure statement’s contents (that information is captured in registration statements).
The expenditure statement requirements do not call for a description of the employer's business nature; they call for reporting expenditures and totals.
Nothing in the expenditure statement provisions requires disclosure of the employer’s major financial contributors.

When expenditures are made for the benefit of specified officials, the filer must state the recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client—an itemization requirement for reportable expenditures.

Registration statements require names/addresses of agents and employers and listing specific bills or resolutions, but do not require naming bill sponsors or legislative members associated with the legislation.
